batch_strategy: Correct the m36 pure-EA candidate identifier to 71d8b719ba209d117b05 and retain the same scientific batch. Freeze these 32 distinct supplied candidate IDs and their supplied predictions before measurement. Use controlled ratio curves to distinguish genuine endpoint-specific responses from interpolation artifacts, extend newly established phenolic-carbonyl baselines, and make two targeted m81 repeats after recent repeats weakened its deterministic loading interpretation. Quantile spans and CW distances inform coverage judgments without being treated as calibrated epistemic uncertainty.

choices.reason: m91 at 1/1 and 141.2 mg predicts an inverted 10.57/9.30 mL interval. Measured same-loading 5/1 record 26c1e0e617e6dbe06ef7 gives 6.91/10.54 mL. Together with the selected 2/1 row, this tests whether the model has misplaced onset in an uncovered early diester response.

m91 at 2/1 matches the selected 1/1 conditions and also predicts V2 below V1, 10.02/9.53 mL. Measured 5/1 and 20/1 anchors 26c1e0e617e6dbe06ef7 and 93f10a8edf06f7acae26 constrain the later curve. The pair can teach endpoint coupling rather than merely shift both endpoints.

Bicyclic acrylate m23 under pure EA at 98.6 mg anchors the selected fixed-loading early comparison. Recent m15 baselines in 2e714d4f0dc73256dd0b and be1d1eac10cca873e4ef rejected large predicted strong-eluent completions, making direct baseline measurement useful for transfer to this sterically different acrylate.

m23 at 1/1 and 98.6 mg supplies an anchor between the selected pure-EA baseline and inverted 5/1 prediction. Lower-loading 1/1 observation 2928443b881ac6713786 measured 6.04/8.50 mL. This separates baseline and loading transfer from a localized response error.

m23 at 5/1 predicts 6.95/5.97 mL, an inconsistent interval under the target definitions. The selected pure-EA and 1/1 rows hold loading conditions fixed. Recent ordered outcomes for inverted m18 and m16 predictions, 2631e65cfde93b7bbd64 and 662cdf5c5a8b351d8584, motivate testing this remaining acrylate failure signature.

m152 at 2/1 and 109.1 mg predicts nearly coincident reversed endpoints, 7.27/7.21 mL. Same-loading pure-EA and 1/1 observations 7da8f3ac36bcb53605d1 and 0f0ce675d00176813bf5 have ordered intervals near 5.3/8.2 mL. This tests an unexplained onset excursion in a hydrophobic aryloxy compound.

m152 at 5/1 matches the selected 2/1 conditions and predicts a larger inversion, 7.72/6.36 mL. Measured 1/1 anchor 0f0ce675d00176813bf5 and 20/1 anchor e8a5f7b2a0bffe5c07f2 bracket the region. Two adjacent labels distinguish a local anomaly from a broader endpoint-response mismatch.

m149 at 1/1 and 100 mg begins a controlled early pair, predicting 7.56/11.46 mL before the selected 2/1 inversion. Its measured 50/1 reference 616dd888d5b03ea79005 is at 150 mg and does not establish the early curve. This adds useful coverage for a non-donor halogenated aromatic environment.

m149 at 2/1 and 100 mg predicts 10.21/9.90 mL: onset moves later while completion falls from the selected 1/1 prediction. Measuring both directly tests this unusual response and extends the inversion diagnostic beyond esters, without replacing new labels with an assumed ordering correction.

Brominated salicylaldehyde m190 under pure EA at 173.7 mg anchors a fixed-loading three-point early curve. Predicted completion is 16.72 mL before falling at 1/1. The newly measured 26.73 mL m197 baseline in ff3ee95fed58907ff8b3 makes substituent-specific strong-eluent baselines a concrete learning question.

m190 at 1/1 matches the selected pure-EA and 2/1 settings and predicts the completion minimum, 11.86 mL. Genuine early declines in m197 and m105 coexist with failed declines in other families. This middle label tests the proposed minimum instead of inferring it from related structures.

m190 at 2/1 completes the fixed-loading early curve, predicting 4.85/14.04 mL. Same-loading 5/1 observation f5259e3f51c168c59973 gives 6.16/19.70 mL. The four-condition sequence can separate an early baseline decline from subsequent solvent-ratio growth.

Positional brominated analogue m186 under pure EA at 100 mg is predicted to finish at 17.05 mL, versus measured 15.18 mL at matched 2/1 conditions in 43758e84c67aabf44a9f. This supplies a baseline comparison with m190 while retaining their different amounts and loading-solvent volumes.

m197 under pure EA at 57.3 mg tests transfer of the newly established long 114.6 mg baseline, 26.73 mL in ff3ee95fed58907ff8b3. The current prediction transfers that correction to 25.55 mL. A new loading level can determine whether that transfer is justified.

m197 at 2/1 and 57.3 mg pairs with the selected pure-EA baseline. Same-loading 5/1 observation a91850e587e062097c02 finishes at 24.51 mL, while the 114.6 mg 2/1 result 454eb2207b9abc0b2a6d finishes at 25.00 mL. This tests persistence of long early completion across loading.

m117 at 5/1 and 182.145 mg begins a matched pair with the selected 20/1 row. Pure-EA record 3c0e2ce9feb019d1dd30 and 2/1 record 5079d0dfcde65893b224 establish shorter early completions at 121.43 mg. This locates later growth while testing loading transfer.

m117 at 20/1 matches the selected 5/1 conditions and has the highest supplied CW distance percentile. Its predicted 13.97/33.70 mL endpoints bridge lower-loading 10/1 observation 09c2a4beb05ca5c84aab and 121.43 mg 50/1 observation d9c8c8af50a10bf07765. The pair tests the missing ratio-response slope.

m123 at 10/1 and 105.3 mg predicts onset at 3.95 mL, earlier than the measured 6.72 mL onset at matched 5/1 conditions in 89d7d7adb1fc72276b1c. Completion is predicted to increase. This tests a later endpoint-specific reversal after recent ether measurements rejected several early completion dips.

m123 at 20/1 matches the selected 10/1 conditions and predicts onset rebounding to 9.84 mL. The pair and measured 5/1 record 89d7d7adb1fc72276b1c distinguish a localized onset minimum from an interpolation artifact. Higher-loading 20/1 record ba56f0e652a97bcee1b2 supplies another reference.

m116 at 5/1 and 105.1 mg follows the newly measured growing early curve in 0a974fa5ccff4ce25b98, 3a6530d37524751b978e and 17418a1ba5c9443057c3. Predicted completion is 10.39 mL, slightly below the measured 2/1 value of 11.21 mL. This tests whether a smaller later decline remains.

m116 at 10/1 matches the selected 5/1 conditions but predicts earlier onset, 4.43 versus 6.33 mL, alongside longer completion. The pair extends an anchored early curve and provides a substitution comparison with m123's predicted 10/1 onset minimum.

m200 under pure EA at 64.585 mg fills the baseline before matched 1/1 and 2/1 observations 97318de99bab4460cf4e and a92f7617b135de150588, measured at 15.15/37.40 and 33.88/74.44 mL. The predicted 4.87/12.32 mL baseline tests where this nitro-alcohol's steep early response begins.

Amino-acetophenone m36 under pure EA at 38.5 mg precedes matched 1/1 and 2/1 observations 762190c8d9f5b2d1a89a and 183af335033005f96b97. The predicted 7.59/15.62 mL baseline tests early adsorption response in an amino-carbonyl environment and broadens baseline learning beyond phenolic compounds.

Ortho-methyl ketone m44 under pure EA at 102.6 mg predicts completion at 13.88 mL, above the matched 2/1 measurement of 8.32 mL in a241f53a141f7c39ed74. m33 supplies a measured precedent for a decline, whereas m29 and m38 supply counterexamples. This baseline discriminates structure-specific transfer.

m44 at 5/1 matches the selected pure-EA conditions and measured 2/1 record a241f53a141f7c39ed74. Predicted completion recovers to 11.50 mL. The resulting three-point comparison tests a genuine intermediate minimum and teaches V2 curvature independently of onset.

m42 at 2/1 and 103 mg predicts completion at 9.14 mL, below the matched 1/1 measurement of 13.02 mL in a2cf80002cbf3b59eefe and near its pure-EA baseline in e81cfc3293405e5d558f. This missing point tests whether the parent ketone shares any early decline with methyl-substituted analogues.

m29 at 1/1 and 97.5 mg predicts a completion maximum of 12.93 mL between measured pure-EA and 2/1 completions of 7.99 and 10.80 mL in 18355dfa0f6e519b7bf6 and e586f782dfd7bb09f66f. This tests the remaining response-shape question after its previously predicted large decline failed.

This exact repeat of m81 at 2/1 and 166.5 mg checks the short 7.93 mL completion in bee82d193ec1ce4fde27 against the recent low-loading 13.00 mL result in 36c9891cc52de490659d. Recent pure-EA and 1/1 repeats disagreed substantially, so reproducibility now takes priority over extending a deterministic loading curve.

This exact repeat of m81 at 20/1 and 111 mg checks the 17.62 mL completion in db2709229820b71e283b. Recent 166.5 mg record 6b8ff4c027d9c4c2d75f finished later, at 23.55 mL, opposite the earlier strong-eluent loading association. The repeat tests whether that apparent ratio-dependent reversal is stable.

m185 under pure EA at 197.55 mg anchors a fixed-loading early curve. The 131.7 mg baseline in 90986ae76102a348680d measured 4.36/8.26 mL. This new loading level is needed to interpret the selected 1/1 maximum without confounding its baseline.

m185 at 1/1 and 197.55 mg predicts completion at 14.37 mL, above the selected 2/1 prediction of 12.12 mL, with a broad single-predictor quantile span. The analogous m191 overshoot failed in ea9c116dcd66aca4039c and e5c683a60b64d9cc299c. This tests the feature in another aldehyde environment.

m185 at 2/1 completes the fixed-loading early curve. Lower-loading 2/1 observation a134ef1942ffcd81d017 finished at 12.36 mL before reaching 19.86 mL at 5/1 in 08ca5c7741cfb5861c5a. The selected pair determines whether a 1/1 maximum is real or the model again overstates the early response.

hypotheses.content: The earlier interpretation of a large, reproducible m81 completion decrease with loading is weakened. Short high-loading records remain at 2/1 and 5/1, but exact repeats at pure EA and 1/1 differ substantially, and the new 20/1 loading contrast points in the opposite direction. A deterministic loading mechanism is not established.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Targeted repeats distinguish transferable ratio-by-loading information from within-tuple variability. This prevents additional labels from reinforcing an overly strong loading correction, particularly for V2 when V1 changes much less.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the 166.5 mg 2/1 repeat retain short completion, and does the 111 mg 20/1 repeat preserve the apparent reversal relative to 166.5 mg?

hypotheses.content: Early aryl-ketone completion declines can be real, but their shape depends on recorded loading and structural environment. m33 declines at 99.7 mg and across parts of the 149.55 mg curve, while its 49.85 mg pure-EA-to-1/1 response rises. Related m29 and m38 curves do not justify transferring a common decline.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The m44, m42 and m29 experiments discriminate different response shapes using existing anchors. They can improve substitution-sensitive ratio response without imposing monotonic completion or making V1 and V2 move together.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m44 have a pure-EA-to-2/1 decline followed by recovery, does m42 completion fall at 2/1, and is m29's predicted 1/1 maximum measured?

hypotheses.content: Recent neutral ether and ester measurements reject a shared large early completion-dip interpretation. m116 rises through pure EA, 1/1 and 2/1; m110 rises from 1/1 to 2/1; m15 has short pure-EA completion at both measured amounts. m127 retains a modest 1/1 minimum, illustrating that local responses still matter. Predicted later onset reversals for m116 and m123 remain unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Extending anchored ether curves into adjacent ratios tests whether remaining curvature belongs to onset, completion, or neither. This provides new response information after the early baselines have become measured anchors.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the predicted 10/1 onset minima in m116 and m123 reproduce at fixed loading, and does m116 completion actually decline slightly at 5/1?

hypotheses.content: Remaining V2-below-V1 predictions for m91, m23, m149 and m152 may indicate failures of the learned joint endpoint response. Previously selected inverted predictions for m18, m16 and higher-loading m75 yielded ordinary ordered measured intervals. This supports testing the diagnostic, but does not establish errors for the new candidates or justify automatically replacing inconsistent catalog labels.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Controlled local labels can repair onset/completion coupling and reduce transfer of exceptional observations across neutral ester and halogenated-aromatic rows. The acquisition signal is endpoint inconsistency and response shape; elution interval width is not uncertainty.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which remaining inverted predictions yield ordinary intervals, and do their errors arise from a misplaced onset, an underestimated completion, or both?

hypotheses.content: Strong-eluent completion differs substantially across the supplied ortho donor-carbonyl environments. m197's newly measured pure-EA completion remains long and near its 1/1–2/1 values; m105 has a shorter declining early response, and m117 has a shorter pure-EA baseline followed by growth at 2/1. Substitution and loading conditions may both contribute. Intramolecular hydrogen bonding remains a chemical prior rather than a demonstrated cause.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The brominated analogues, lower-loading m197 pair and matched m117 extension test structural baselines and ratio slopes separately. These comparisons can improve functional and positional transfer beyond coarse donor/acceptor counts while preserving recorded condition differences.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m186 and m190 reproduce their predicted early completion declines, does m197 retain its long baseline at 57.3 mg, and where does m117's 5/1-to-20/1 growth occur at fixed loading?

hypotheses.content: The predicted m185 curve at 197.55 mg may contain a spurious 1/1 completion maximum: supplied V2 predictions are approximately 8.71, 14.37 and 12.12 mL at pure EA, 1/1 and 2/1. No measurement at these selected settings establishes that maximum.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A fixed-loading three-point curve distinguishes a baseline error from an intermediate overshoot and loading transfer. It addresses a response-shape failure demonstrated by the recent m191 experiment without assuming that failure recurs in m185.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Is m185 completion at 1/1 genuinely above its matched 2/1 completion, or does the measured early curve grow through both ratios?

feedback_interpretation: Recent outcomes weaken several previous interpretations while preserving compound-specific exceptions. For m81, the pure-EA 111 mg repeat finished at 9.28 mL instead of the earlier 14.64 mL, and the 1/1 166.5 mg repeat finished at 12.78 mL instead of 6.66 mL. These differences weaken a large deterministic loading effect. The new 166.5 mg 20/1 completion of 23.55 mL also exceeds the earlier 111 mg value of 17.62 mL, motivating two discriminating repeats. For m33, the 49.85 mg pure-EA-to-1/1 completion rose from 12.53 to 16.76 mL; at 149.55 mg, completion was 11.68 at 1/1, 14.02 at 2/1 and 12.03 at 5/1. Its response remains loading-specific. The m116 early curve increased from 7.92 through 8.57 to 11.21 mL, and m110 increased from 9.10 to 9.52 mL between 1/1 and 2/1. Their predicted declines failed. m127 retained a modest minimum, but its 2/1 result of 4.99/11.66 mL was much earlier than its acquisition prediction. Both m15 pure-EA completions were short, 7.57 and 6.93 mL, rejecting the proposed long baseline across loading. m191's 1/1 completions of 17.73 and 19.49 mL were below matched 2/1 values of 21.00 and 23.74 mL, rejecting the proposed overshoot. Conversely, m197's pure-EA completion of 26.73 mL exposed a major baseline underprediction and extends its coherent long early-completion region. m105 declined from 10.31 under pure EA to 8.13 at 1/1 before reaching 8.87 at 2/1, so a blanket monotonic rule would be inappropriate. Finally, inverted m18, m16 and higher-loading m75 predictions yielded ordered labels; m75's exceptional low-loading 2/1 interval did not transfer to 109.5 mg. These outcomes motivate controlled tests of remaining inversions. All acquisition errors discussed here are historical, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The 32 experiments target concrete ways the predictor can generalize incorrectly across remaining Row conditions. Nine rows test endpoint inconsistencies through local comparisons in a diester, a bicyclic acrylate and two halogenated aromatic environments. Eight rows extend the revised phenolic-carbonyl interpretation through a controlled m190 early curve, an m186 baseline, a lower-loading m197 pair and a matched m117 ratio extension. Four ether rows test later endpoint-specific curvature after recent early curves became measured anchors. Four related ketone rows discriminate minima, maxima and baseline differences using existing fixed-loading observations. Three m185 rows test a predicted intermediate maximum after the m191 maximum failed. Two donor-containing baseline rows anchor steep early responses outside the phenolic series. The two m81 repeats deliberately have low coverage novelty: their value is resolving reproducibility after previous evidence changed. Multiple rows per molecule provide controlled response information; no condition tuple is selected twice within this batch. Expected benefits are better learning of structural baselines, ratio curvature, endpoint coupling and the limits of loading transfer across related candidate rows. Quantile spans are uncalibrated outputs of one predictor, and CW distance describes supplied feature-space coverage. Missing experimental variables constrain causal explanations, so the plan seeks useful predictive relationships without assigning unobserved mechanisms or optimizing chromatographic performance.
